actions.action: Replace chat-based inference with one shared key-status panel.
actions.mechanism: Separate the last confirmed holder from any unresolved transfer.
actions.implementation: Give both volunteers access to a shared page showing last confirmed holder, confirmation time, pending recipient, and pending-since time. Initialize it only after one volunteer confirms possession.
actions.check: After an initiated but unaccepted transfer, both volunteers see the same last confirmed holder and a clearly unresolved handoff.
actions.risk: A last confirmed holder may not physically possess the key; label it explicitly rather than implying certainty.

actions.action: Require the receiving volunteer to acknowledge each handoff.
actions.mechanism: Use a two-step transfer rather than treating a sent message as proof of receipt.
actions.implementation: The holder selects “Hand key over,” recording the stated handoff time and creating a pending transfer. The other volunteer selects “Received” to become the confirmed holder. Store acknowledgment time separately.
actions.check: Starting a transfer alone never changes the confirmed holder; acceptance changes it and resolves exactly that transfer.
actions.risk: Forgotten acknowledgments leave completed physical transfers unresolved.

actions.mechanism: Preserve an auditable sequence instead of overwriting disputed details.
actions.implementation: Record each transfer with sender, recipient, handoff time, submission time, and status. Show timestamps with timezone. Corrections append a linked amendment with author and reason rather than deleting the original.
actions.check: Correct an incorrectly entered handoff time; verify that both the original and amended time remain visible and attributable.
actions.risk: Manual handoff times can still be inaccurate; submission timestamps must not be presented as physical-transfer times.

actions.mechanism: Validate each update against the current shared state.
actions.implementation: Allow only the confirmed holder to initiate a transfer, only to the other volunteer, and only when none is pending. Use atomic version checks and unique request IDs so stale screens and repeated taps cannot create extra transfers.
actions.check: Submit two initiation requests concurrently and retry one request; exactly one pending transfer exists.
actions.risk: Strict validation can block legitimate recovery after a mistaken entry; provide an explicit correction route.

actions.action: Provide an “Uncertain or disputed” recovery path.
actions.mechanism: Represent missing knowledge instead of forcing a potentially false holder assignment.
actions.implementation: Let either volunteer flag a transfer as disputed or report the key missing. Retain the last confirmed holder as historical information. Resolve through a possession statement by one volunteer and acknowledgment by the other, recording resolution time separately from any known handoff time.
actions.check: Dispute a pending transfer; it remains visibly unresolved until both volunteers complete recovery, with no fabricated handoff timestamp.
actions.risk: If neither volunteer can locate the key, the system can expose uncertainty but cannot resolve it.

actions.action: Surface overdue acknowledgments to the two volunteers.
actions.mechanism: Make unresolved work visible without interpreting silence as acceptance.
actions.implementation: Agree on an acknowledgment interval. When a pending transfer exceeds it, display an overdue badge and send one reminder to each volunteer linking to that transfer. Never automatically assign the recipient as holder.
actions.check: Leave a test transfer pending beyond the interval; both volunteers receive a reminder, while holder and unresolved status remain unchanged.
actions.risk: Reminders may be ignored or become noise; keep them bounded and stop them once resolved.
